decision_rule: Gate v2 on the OOS window only, one read through qe.gateway.load(id,'oos'): pass iff (1) one-sided t of the net-1x per-event P&L (day-clustered; stationary/day-cluster bootstrap >= 430,000 draws) >= 3.6807; (2) net-2x mean > 0 (criterion 3); (3) criteria 4 and 7 of PARAMETERS.md (years, concentration, terciles, +-25% neighbours on entry/exit times or thresholds, one-bar delay) pass; (4) Red Team and re-implementation sign-off; (5) hold-out read in the restated one-sided tolerance form with h = decay_haircut. Anything else is 'refuted' or 'near-miss' (near-miss = t >= 2.0 with criterion 3 passed); the result file prints criterion-4 power and the joint figure for its own OOS length. Derivative rule (D-009): the evidence displays 2008-2026, so the decision window is 1990-01-02..2007-12-31 only; 2008-2016 rows in the file are never read for this row.
hypothesis: A pre-registered hypothesis under test, not an edge claim. Sharp two-day falls in crude-oil complex futures are partly liquidity-driven (margin calls, CTA de-risking, index-roll timing) and partly revert within 1-3 sessions; on FTMO terms an energy long carries roll yield through the swap, so the holding cost is not the headwind it is for index CFDs (closed G2). Sign fixed: long after the fall.
rules: Daily excess-return series r_t of the listed roots in daily_futures_1984_2016 (US close-to-close, roll inside the series). Price index P_t = cumulative product of (1 + r_t). Signal at close of day t: R2_t = r_{t-1} + r_t (two-day return); sigma2_t = sqrt(2) x s.d.(r) over days t-59..t (60 observations, at least 50 non-missing). If R2_t < -2 x sigma2_t and no position is open in that root, BUY at the close of day t+1 (one-day delay: daily data has no open, and a fill at the signal close would be look-ahead). EXIT at the close of the first day u >= t+2 on which P_u > mean(P_{u-4..u}) (5-day mean of the index), or at the close of day t+4 at the latest (3 sessions after entry). No pyramiding, one position per root, no stops (the FTMO 5%/10% guard is applied by the portfolio layer, guard_fraction). Days with |r| > 25% (the inherited loader's listed bad days) are set to missing before the signal.
parameters: roots CL, CO, HO (WTI, Brent, heating oil); trigger 2-day return < -2 sigma (60-day); entry next close; exit first close above 5-day mean or after 3 sessions
instruments: FTMO USOIL.cash, UKOIL.cash, HEATOIL CFDs (tested on CL, CO, HO futures excess returns)
vol_scaler: per root weight = 0.10/sqrt(252) / EWMA (com 60 days) s.d. of r through the signal day; roots equally risk-weighted (divide by 3); no cap.
cost_model: 1x floors per briefs/00-common.md: 2.5 bp per side (WTI floor applied to all three energy CFDs) + financing markup 3%/yr per calendar day held (FTMO swap = roll yield + markup; the excess-return series already embeds the roll yield, so only the markup is charged; the markup is an assumption to be replaced by the Rules Keeper's swap file). 2x run attached (5 bp per side, 6%/yr).
notes: Source: candidates.md rank 27 (SC C-8-06, absorbs P-C16/P-C24). EVIDENCE WINDOW: Quantified Strategies USO 2008-2026 (paywalled rules, in-sample) and blog CL/GC 2008-2026 -> derivative for 2008+; decided on 1990-2007 which no cited evidence displays. Closed family: G2-01..07 (RSI(2)/3-down dip buy on index CFDs) is the same rule class on other markets; commodities were not in G2 -> new markets, not a re-run. Institutional change dates: 2004-2008 commodity financialization inside the late OOS (sub-period 1990-2003 vs 2004-2007 reported), 2026-01-30 FTMO rolling contracts (affects the cost model only). OOS 18 years: bar 0.87; criterion-4 power 1.00 at true Sharpe 1.5. Realistic: claimed +40..100 bp per hold, 20-50 bp after haircut, vs about 500 bp s.d. over 3 sessions, about 25-30 trades/yr pooled with energy correlation 0.8 -> annual Sharpe about 0.2-0.4 -> power under 0.15. Economics: 20-50 bp after haircut vs 5 bp round trip + about 2.5 bp markup = 3-7x: passes the screen. Carver: turnover about 30 round trips/yr x 7.5 bp = 2.3%/yr vs about 15% sleeve vol = 0.15 Sharpe units, under one third of any pre-cost Sharpe that could pass. Red Team strongest objection: the only evidence is an in-sample, paywalled blog on 2008-2026; 1990-2007 crude had different participants (pre-financialization), so a null result there does not refute the 2008+ claim and a pass there does not confirm it - answerable only by stating, as here, that the row tests 1990-2007 and the hold-out (2025-2026) is the bridge.
